title: Upsert Inventory
statement:
A shipment just arrived at the warehouse. Some of its products are already in stock and some are new. Add the whole shipment to the inventory with one `INSERT` statement, then list the inventory.

The `inventory` table has one row per product:

- `sku`: the product code, the primary key
- `name`: the product name
- `quantity`: how many are in stock

The `shipment` table has the same three columns, with each `sku` at most once.

For every shipment row, add a new inventory row when its `sku` is not in stock yet. When it is, add the shipment's `quantity` to the quantity already in stock and keep the inventory's name. Then return `sku`, `name`, and `quantity` for every inventory row, ordered by `sku`.

Expected output:

```text
INSERT 0 3

  sku   |        name        | quantity
--------+--------------------+----------
 BK-101 | Hardcover notebook |       40
 BK-205 | Spiral notebook    |       45
 MK-020 | Highlighter set    |       25
 PN-310 | Gel pen, black     |      120
 PN-315 | Gel pen, blue      |      100
 ST-500 | Stapler            |        8
(6 rows)
```

hints: Insert from a `SELECT` on the shipment table, then decide what happens when a `sku` already exists.
`ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE` runs instead of the insert for an existing `sku`. Inside it, `EXCLUDED` is the row you tried to insert.

sql.starter:
-- TODO: add every shipment row to inventory, adding to the quantity
-- when the sku is already in stock

SELECT sku, name, quantity
FROM inventory
ORDER BY sku;
sql.solution:
INSERT INTO inventory (sku, name, quantity)
SELECT sku, name, quantity
FROM shipment
ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE
SET quantity = inventory.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity;

SELECT sku, name, quantity
FROM inventory
ORDER BY sku;
